claim: Anthropic proposes presenting MCP servers as code APIs (files in a ./servers/ tree) that the agent calls from a code execution environment instead of direct tool calls.
quote: a solution is to present MCP servers as code APIs rather than direct tool calls
title: Code execution with MCP: Building more efficient agents

claim: Anthropic's own illustrative example (self-reported, not a benchmarked eval): progressive disclosure via filesystem exploration cut tool-definition tokens from 150,000 to 2,000, a stated 98.7% saving.
quote: This reduces the token usage from 150,000 tokens to 2,000 tokens
title: Code execution with MCP: Building more efficient agents

claim: Anthropic says intermediate results otherwise pass through the model; for a 2-hour sales meeting transcript this could mean an extra 50,000 tokens (illustrative estimate).
quote: For a 2-hour sales meeting, that could mean processing an additional 50,000 tokens.
title: Code execution with MCP: Building more efficient agents

claim: Anthropic states code execution needs a sandbox, resource limits and monitoring, adding operational overhead and security considerations that direct tool calls avoid, and that benefits must be weighed against these costs.
quote: These infrastructure requirements add operational overhead and security considerations that direct tool calls avoid.
title: Code execution with MCP: Building more efficient agents

claim: Anthropic says conditional logic executed in code saves time-to-first-token latency versus having the model evaluate each if-statement.
quote: being able to write out a conditional tree that gets executed also saves on
title: Code execution with MCP: Building more efficient agents

claim: Privacy: the MCP client can tokenize PII so real values flow between MCP tools without passing through the model.
quote: The real email addresses, phone numbers, and names flow from Google Sheets to Salesforce, but never through the model.
title: Code execution with MCP: Building more efficient agents

claim: Anthropic credits Cloudflare with similar findings under the name Code Mode.
quote: Cloudflare published similar findings
title: Code execution with MCP: Building more efficient agents

claim: Anthropic's advanced-tool-use post: at Anthropic, tool definitions have consumed 134K tokens before optimization; a 5-server setup of 58 tools used about 55K tokens (self-reported).
quote: At Anthropic, we've seen tool definitions consume 134K tokens before optimization.
title: Introducing advanced tool use on the Claude Developer Platform

claim: Tool Search Tool, internal testing (self-reported): context for ~50+ MCP tools fell from ~77K to ~8.7K tokens (85% reduction).

title: Introducing advanced tool use on the Claude Developer Platform

claim: Programmatic Tool Calling example: 200KB of raw expense data reduced to 1KB reaching Claude's context (illustrative example).
quote: reducing consumption from 200KB of raw expense data to just 1KB of results.
title: Introducing advanced tool use on the Claude Developer Platform

claim: PTC measured on complex research tasks (internal): average tokens dropped from 43,588 to 27,297, a 37% reduction.
quote: Average usage dropped from 43,588 to 27,297 tokens, a 37% reduction on complex research tasks.
title: Introducing advanced tool use on the Claude Developer Platform

claim: PTC accuracy (internal): knowledge retrieval 25.6% to 28.5%; GIA benchmarks 46.5% to 51.2%.

claim: Anthropic says 20+ tool calls in one code block eliminate 19+ inference passes (latency claim, arithmetic not a timed measurement).

claim: Anthropic recommends PTC for large datasets needing only aggregates, workflows with 3+ dependent calls, filtering/transforming results, and parallel operations; it adds a code execution step overhead.

claim: Anthropic recommends Tool Search when definitions exceed 10K tokens, with accuracy issues, multiple MCP servers, 10+ tools; it adds a search step and latency.
quote: The feature adds a search step before tool invocation, so it delivers the best ROI when the context savings and accuracy improvements outweigh additional latency.

claim: Tool Use Examples improved complex-parameter accuracy from 72% to 90% in Anthropic internal testing, at the cost of extra definition tokens.

claim: Cloudflare (Sept 2025) introduced Code Mode: convert MCP tools into a TypeScript API and have the LLM write code that calls it.
quote: Convert the MCP tools into a TypeScript API, and then ask an LLM to write code that calls that API.
title: Code Mode: the better way to use MCP

claim: Cloudflare says chaining in code avoids routing every intermediate output through the LLM; claims LLMs are better at writing code to call MCP than calling MCP directly (assertion, no benchmark in the post).
quote: In short, LLMs are better at writing code to call MCP, than at calling MCP directly.
title: Code Mode: the better way to use MCP

claim: Cloudflare Code Mode runs code in a V8 isolate sandbox with no Internet access; only access is via TypeScript APIs for connected MCP servers.
quote: The sandbox is totally isolated from the Internet.
title: Code Mode: the better way to use MCP

claim: Cloudflare in Sept 2025 loaded the entire generated TypeScript API into context; dynamic browsing was future work. Worker Loader pricing not yet finalized.
quote: Currently, the entire API is loaded, but future improvements could allow an agent to search and browse the API more dynamically
title: Code Mode: the better way to use MCP

claim: Cloudflare MCP server for the full Cloudflare API: two tools search() and execute() consume about 1,000 tokens; 99.9% input-token reduction vs an equivalent native MCP server that would use 1.17 million tokens (tiktoken-measured, self-reported).
quote: An equivalent MCP server without Code Mode would consume 1.17 million tokens
title: Code Mode: give agents an entire API in 1,000 tokens

claim: Cloudflare runs generated code in a Dynamic Worker isolate: V8 sandbox, no file system, no env vars, external fetches disabled by default.
quote: a lightweight V8 sandbox with no file system, no environment variables to leak through prompt injection and external fetches disabled by default
title: Code Mode: give agents an entire API in 1,000 tokens

claim: Cloudflare states client-side Code Mode requires the agent to ship with secure sandbox access (tradeoff).
quote: The tradeoff is that it requires the agent to ship with secure sandbox access.
title: Code Mode: give agents an entire API in 1,000 tokens

claim: Cloudflare criticizes dynamic tool search: it needs a maintained and evaluated search function and each matched tool still uses tokens.
quote: now requires a search function that must be maintained and evaluated, and each matched tool still uses tokens
title: Code Mode: give agents an entire API in 1,000 tokens

claim: Cloudflare internal portal: 4 MCP servers expose 52 tools using about 9,400 tokens of definitions; with Code Mode they collapse to 2 portal tools about 600 tokens (94% reduction, self-reported).
quote: those 52 tools collapse into 2 portal tools consuming roughly 600 tokens
title: Scaling MCP adoption: reference architecture

claim: Cloudflare changelog 2026-03-26: MCP server portals support Code Mode; portal exposes a single code tool, generated JavaScript runs in an isolated Dynamic Worker.
quote: the portal exposes a single `code` tool instead of listing every tool from every upstream MCP server
title: Code Mode for MCP server portals (changelog)
